name: Home Design 3D Outdoor/Garden (Anuman/Microids)
price: Free download but paid-gated: $4.99 'Full' unlock plus IAPs; users report being told to also buy the $6.99 base Home Design 3D app to get save/multi-level after already paying for Gold
complaints: Paid Gold users asked to purchase the separate base app to unlock save and multi-level functions
Items randomly move or delete themselves; no way to lock an item or layer
No support for sloped land, raised/sunken gardens, paths, driveways, or roofs in a garden design app; 'pitiful' plant/element selection
App recently started crashing once or twice a day; effectively abandoned by Anuman/Microids (~90 downloads/day residual)
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: free AI garden-design apps and Planner 5D exist, but none combine offline 2D/3D garden planning with real plant libraries and one-time pricing; most competitors are subscription AI-photo gimmicks
moatNotes: Low moat — pure client-side 3D editor, no network infrastructure needed. Content moat is the 3D asset/plant library, which is buildable. The 33k ratings at 2.29 stars prove a large paying audience the incumbent actively burned

name: Home Design 3D (main app, Anuman/Microids)
price: Free demo, paid-gated: Gold/Gold Plus IAP unlocks (~$7-$10) required to save projects and access floors
complaints: Last Android update January 11, 2024 (~2.5 years stale as of mid-2026); users call it 'abandonware' with feature requests years old and no action
Crashes during long sessions destroy unsaved work — fatal in a design tool whose save function is itself paywalled
High battery drain on older devices, pricey stacked IAPs on top of the original paid unlock
Developer support slow and sometimes not in English
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium-high: Planner 5D and Room Planner are large freemium incumbents, but both are aggressive subscription paywalls that users equally resent; a one-time-purchase, offline, reliable-save clone directly counters both failure modes
moatNotes: Moat is the furniture/asset catalog and 3D engine polish — months of asset work, no server moat. Still ~52k downloads/30 days on a dead app = proven ongoing demand

name: eMeals - Meal Planning Recipes
price: Paid-gated: subscription-only service (~$59.99/yr or ~$12.99/mo) after 14-day free trial; app is useless without subscription
complaints: Cannot cancel online — must phone customer service during limited hours; users report continued billing after attempted cancellation
Free trial silently converts to a full ANNUAL charge; strict no-refund policy ('too bad' responses); only 4% of support callers report resolution (PissedConsumer)
Android app abandoned: last update March 22, 2024 (~2+ years stale) while still charging subscribers
BBB/Trustpilot pages dominated by billing complaints rather than product complaints — the meal-planning value itself is what keeps people paying
freeIncumbentRisk: Medium: free recipe apps abound, but curated weekly dinner plans + auto grocery-cart handoff (Walmart/Instacart) is what people pay eMeals for; Mealime/Samsung Food cover only part of it. Yummly's 2024 shutdown and Pepperplate's death also freed up meal-planning refugees
moatNotes: Real moat is the human/AI-curated weekly menu content pipeline and grocery-API integrations — moderate effort, no network effect. A transparent-billing, cancel-anytime clone weaponizes their #1 complaint

name: F-Secure FREEDOME VPN
price: Paid-gated: subscription VPN (~$35-50/yr), no permanent free tier
complaints: Standalone Freedome declared end-of-life (transition began April 2024; EOL after May 22, 2024); Android app last updated June 26, 2024
F-Secure's Jan 2, 2025 backend change deliberately broke older Freedome/Total VPN apps — stuck on 'Connecting…' — stranding paying users mid-subscription
Paying subscribers force-migrated into the bigger F-Secure Total bundle/app they didn't choose
Long-time fans (privacy-conscious, EU-based, anti-US-VPN crowd) publicly hunting for replacements on F-Secure community and MalwareTips
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Proton VPN's free tier and well-run paid rivals (Mullvad, Windscribe) absorb refugees; a new entrant can't compete on price alone
moatNotes: CAUTION: real infrastructure moat — global server fleet, ongoing opex, trust/reputation are the product; this is NOT a solo-dev clone target unless built as a reseller/white-label, and the trust deficit favors established brands. Included as demand evidence more than a build target

_note: Investigated but rejected (failed rubric): Paprika 3 Android (4.87, actively updated), ChefTap (4.48, dying but users still happy), BigOven (4.65), mSecure (4.68 despite forced-sub anger), Enpass (anger exists but Play rating too high), Magicplan (4.2, 10M — just above threshold), AppLock/DoMobile (4.23), Construction Master Pro (4.76), iScape Android (4.36 but only 130 ratings), SplashID (3.37 but ratings base too thin to verify 100K+ on current package).
